Q3-084-M01.question: Does generic live-authority lookup return the PARTIAL patch record itself?

Q3-084-M02.question: Does a live implementation surface changed by a PARTIAL patch resolve independently through its own authority role?
Q3-084-M02.answer: YES. scripts/global_validate.py resolves independently as VALIDATION_INVOCATION_AUTHORITY; Patch 002 also references a separate LIVE core rule by file content.

Q3-084-M03.question: Would excluding all PARTIAL patch records from live lookup suppress any legitimate live authority?
Q3-084-M03.answer: YES, or at minimum it would risk conflating patch-record history with independently governed live effects. PARTIAL is too heterogeneous for a blanket rule.

Q3-084-M04.question: Is authority_effect already sufficient to distinguish non-authoritative patch records from bounded authority-changing patches?
Q3-084-M04.answer: PARTIALLY. It is sufficient for Patch 002, but not for Patch 055 because no authority_effect field is present there.

Q3-084-M05.question: Are there PARTIAL records with authority_effect NONE whose affected implementation surfaces are nevertheless legitimately live?
Q3-084-M05.answer: YES. Patch 002 explicitly has authority_effect NONE while separately registering a LIVE core rule and inventory artifacts that describe already-live authority sources.

unsafe_generalizations: PARTIAL does not automatically mean live authority.
PARTIAL does not automatically mean non-live record.
Excluding all PARTIAL patch records from lookup would be overbroad because it would collapse distinct work-status, accounting, and effect-status meanings.
A patch record can remain PARTIAL while independently governed implementation surfaces are already live.
authority_effect NONE on a patch record does not imply that every related surface is non-live; it only constrains the patch record itself.
